title: Agitation
description: During the brewing process, the relative movement of coffee powder and water is increased through water flow impact or artificial stirring, thereby accelerating extraction.

title: Blooming
description: The first step to brewing coffee by hand. Inject water to moisten the coffee grounds to expel carbon dioxide and make subsequent extraction more even.

title: Burr Grinder
description: A grinder that uses two toothed blades to "chop" or "crush" coffee beans is the core equipment for specialty coffee.

title: Bypass
description: When brewing, the hot water does not pass through the coffee powder bed, but flows directly from the edge of the filter paper into the lower pot, which will dilute the coffee concentration.

title: Channeling
description: The hot water seeks the path of least resistance in the coffee grounds, causing some of the coffee grounds to be over-extracted and other parts to be under-extracted.

title: Crema
description: The golden-yellow layer of emulsified oil on the surface of espresso coffee, filled with tiny bubbles.

title: Extraction Yield
description: The proportion by weight of the substance in the coffee grounds that is dissolved by the hot water and carried into the cup. The ideal extraction rate is usually between 18% and 22%.

title: Fines
description: The tiny powder that is inevitably produced when grinding coffee beans. They have a huge impact on extraction flow rate and flavor.

title: Grinding particle size distribution (Grind Distribution) Analysis: The influence of uniformity on channeling effect
description: Explore how grinder disc geometry affects the particle size distribution (PSD) of coffee grounds. An in-depth analysis of how too high a ratio of fines to coarse powders can cause channeling and lead to extremely uneven coffee extraction.

title: Maillard Reaction
description: The most important chemical reaction in the coffee roasting process. Amino acids and reducing sugars produce complex brown polymers and aroma molecules when heated.

title: The golden cross of light, medium and dark roasts: the dynamic relationship between roast level and optimal brewing temperature
description: The roasting process of coffee beans not only changes the color, but also completely changes the microstructure of the cells. In-depth analysis of why light roasting requires high temperature and dark roasting requires low temperature, and how to find the optimal extraction temperature curve for different bean types.

title: Total Dissolved Solids (TDS)
description: Total Dissolved Solids. It represents the proportion of coffee substances and the proportion of water in a cup of coffee liquid, which determines the concentration of coffee.

title: Fluid mechanics of three-stage water injection method: scientific principles of steaming, main extraction and tail stage
description: Why does hand-brewed coffee need to be filled with water in stages? Deeply analyze the fluid mechanics and chemical extraction mechanism behind the three-stage water injection method, and explore the effects of exhaust and agitation on concentration.

title: The core indicators of specialty coffee: how to accurately control the extraction rate (Extraction Yield)
description: In-depth analysis of the science of coffee extraction, including solubility, the origin of the golden extraction zone (18%-22%), and how to correct over-extraction and under-extraction flavor defects through water temperature, grinding degree and time.

title: Water Chemistry of Specialty Coffee: How TDS, Hardness and pH Determine Flavor
description: Water makes up 98% of the volume of a coffee drink and is the ultimate solvent for coffee extraction. Explore the decisive effects of total dissolved solids (TDS), calcium and magnesium ion hardness, and buffering capacity (Alkalinity) on coffee flavor and acidity.

title: 擾動與攪拌（Agitation）
description: 沖煮時由水柱、攪拌或旋轉造成的粉水運動；適量有助均勻潤濕，過量則可能拖慢流速。

title: 悶蒸（Blooming）
description: 手沖開始時用少量熱水均勻潤濕咖啡粉，讓氣體釋放並為後續注水建立較一致的粉床。

title: 刀盤磨豆機（Burr Grinder）
description: 以兩組刀盤控制咖啡顆粒大小的磨豆機；相較刀片式磨豆機，通常更容易取得穩定、可重現的研磨結果。

title: 旁流與後加水（Bypass）
description: 水沒有通過咖啡粉床便進入成品，或沖煮後刻意加入清水稀釋濃縮咖啡液的做法。

title: 通道效應（Channeling）
description: 水集中穿過粉床中阻力較低的位置，令不同區域的接觸時間與萃取程度不一致。

title: 咖啡油脂（Crema）
description: 義式濃縮咖啡表面的細緻泡沫層，由氣體、咖啡油脂與液體在加壓沖煮後形成。

title: 萃取率（Extraction Yield）
description: 原有咖啡粉重量中，有多少比例的可溶物質進入成品咖啡液；需要飲品重量與 TDS 才能估算。

title: 細粉（Fines）
description: 研磨時產生、明顯小於主要顆粒的咖啡粉；它們增加表面積，也可能移動到濾紙並改變流速。

title: 研磨粒徑分佈：均勻度如何改變手沖流速
description: 從主要顆粒、細粉與大顆粒理解磨豆機的粒徑分佈，並用可重現的沖煮測試判斷應調整研磨還是注水。

title: 梅納反應（Maillard Reaction）
description: 含胺基化合物與還原糖在加熱下發生的一系列反應，會形成顏色、香氣與多種風味物質。

title: 烘焙度與沖煮溫度：建立可調整的起始範圍
description: 理解淺焙與深焙的結構差異，學會用味道與流速逐步調整水溫，而不是套用單一黃金數字。

title: 總溶解固體（TDS）
description: 成品咖啡中溶解物質所佔的質量百分比，常用來表示飲品濃度，但不能單獨代表萃取是否理想。

title: 三階段注水：把總水量拆成可觀察的節奏
description: 從悶蒸、主要注水到尾段，理解累積水量、擾動與水位如何互相影響，並用味道調整每一段。

title: 萃取率實用指南：公式、測量與風味診斷
description: 用成品重量與 TDS 估算萃取率，分清濃度和萃取程度，並建立每次只改一個變數的修正流程。

title: 咖啡沖煮用水：硬度、鹼度與可重現測試
description: 理解礦物質與緩衝能力如何影響萃取和酸質，並用樽裝水標籤、試紙或水質報告建立可比較的沖煮紀錄。
